title: Andy Reid: New York overturned Rashee Rice catch, not a call I agree with
summary: The most pivotal call on Thanksgiving night was a replay review that went against the Chiefs.
content: Chiefs coach Andy Reid was not happy with the NFL's officiating office in New York over a crucial call in the final minutes of the Thanksgiving night loss to the Bills. With the Chiefs facing third-and-10 at their own 9-yard line with 1:51 remaining in the fourth quarter, Patrick Mahomes hit Rashee Rice over the middle for what the officials ruled was a sensational 11-yard catch. But the officiating office reviewed the play and ruled that Rice lost control as he was going to the ground. Reid said after the game that the on-field officials told him they thought it was a catch but the officiating office overruled them. Reid agreed with the officials on the field. "Not one that I agreed with, but they said it came from New York," Reid said. "It's not from these guys, our guys called it a completion — the guys who were working the game. I'm not sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, then his elbow hit, then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally, in those kind of situations, it's got to be clear and obvious. And to me, that was not clear and obvious.” It was a big play, as it went from the Chiefs having first-and-10 at the 20-yard line with all three timeouts and a real chance of driving for a game-winning score on that possession, to the Chiefs having fourth-and-10 at their own 9-yard line and punting the ball back to the Bills. Ultimately, after an exchange of punts, it was the Bills who kicked the game-winning field goal as time expired. And it was Reid left to wonder what might have been if the call on the field had stood.

title: Bills lead Chiefs 7-3 at halftime on Thanksgiving night
summary: Nasty weather in Western New York has limited offensive production for both Buffalo and Kansas City.
content: There is some nasty weather in Western New York for Thanksgiving night and the Bills look like they have a home-field advance over the Chiefs. Buffalo leads Kansas City 7-3 at halftime. With steady freezing rain falling throughout the first half, it was difficult for both teams to get much going offensively. The game-time temperature was 35 degrees but the feels like temperature was down to 21. The Bills have relied on running back James Cook for most of their offensive production. Cook rushed for 71 yards on 19 carries in the first half with a 5-yard touchdown. Josh Allen is just 5-of-10 passing for 41 yards with an interception. Safety Alohi Gilman picked off Allen in the end zone on second-and-8 from the Kansas City 9 midway through the second quarter. At that point, it seemed like if the Bills scored a touchdown, they might have an insurmountable lead. While the Chiefs didn’t score off of that interception, they at least kept Buffalo off the board. But Kansas City had several miscues from the wet ball. The team had trouble fielding kicks, punter Matt Ariza had trouble catching a long snap before a punt, and Patrick Mahomes had trouble fielding a snap. But Kansas City finally got a little something going late in the second quarter, with Harrison Butker sending a 26-yard field goal through the uprights to narrow Buffalo’s lead to four points. Through 30 minutes, Mahomes is 10-of-15 for 97 yards. Travis Kelce has four receptions for 71 yards, including a key 21-yard catch at the end of the first half to get Kansas City into scoring position. The Chiefs will receive the second-half kickoff.

title: Brock Purdy misses practice again on Thursday
summary: The 49ers remained without the leader of their offense at Thursday's practice.
content: The 49ers remained without the leader of their offense at Thursday's practice. Quarterback Brock Purdy missed practice for the second straight day with an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Wednesday that Purdy is day-to-day and that he's not dealing with a high-ankle sprain, but his status for Sunday's game against the Seahawks is definitely questionable after two missed practices in a row. Safety Siran Neal (knee, foot) and wide receiver Jordan Watkins (groin) were also out for the Niners. Wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck), cornerback Deommodore Lenoir (foot), cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder, neck), and guard Carver Willis (illness) were limited participants. Wide receiver Keenan Allen (rest), defensive end Romello Height (hand), defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle), running back Christian McCaffrey (rest), offensive tackle Austen Pleasants (knee), defensive end Mykel Williams (hand), and left tackle Trent Williams (rest) were listed as full participants.

title: Dalton Kincaid active, Christian Benford inactive for Bills-Chiefs
summary: The Bills will have one of their key offensive weapons for tonight's game against the Chiefs, but they won't have a key defender.
content: The Bills will have one of their key offensive weapons for tonight's game against the Chiefs, but they won't have a key defender. Tight end Dalton Kincaid is active for the Thanksgiving matchup while cornerback Christian Benford is inactive. Kincaid was listed as questionable with thumb and ankle injuries. He missed Sunday’s win over the Dolphins. Benford also missed Sunday’s game with a groin injury. For the Chiefs, Kenneth Walker will miss his third straight game with a groin injury as he was ruled out on Wednesday. Buffalo’s inactives are Benford, receiver Skyler Bell, safety Jalon Kilgore, outside linebacker Mike Danna, offensive lineman Jude Bowry, and defensive lineman Greg Gaines. Kansas City’s inactives are Walker, quarterback Garrett Nussmeier, cornerback Melvin Smith, defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott, offensive tackle Diego Pounds, offensive tackle Jaylon Moore, and defensive tackle Marcus Harris.

title: Eagles make a game of it with blocked punt for touchdown
summary: The Eagles are back in it after blocking a punt and returning it for a touchdown in the fourth quarter in Dallas.
content: The Eagles aren't going down without a fight in Dallas today. After falling behind 31-10 late in the third quarter, it appeared that Philadelphia was out of it. But late in the third quarter, Joe Milton hit DeVonta Smith for a 45-yard touchdown pass that made it 31-17. And then early in the fourth quarter, Philadelphia's Ty Robinson blocked a Dallas punt, and Kenny Moore picked it up and walked in to the end zone for a touchdown. It's now 31-24 Cowboys. The Eagles' defense has had trouble containing the Cowboys' offense, but this game is far from over.

title: Eagles mount furious comeback, beat Cowboys 39-38 in Thanksgiving classic
summary: What looked like a blowout turned into a great one, as Philadelphia stormed back to win in Dallas.
content: It was a Thanksgiving Day classic in Dallas. In a wild game that went from an apparent blowout to a thrilling comeback, the Cowboys jumped out to a 31-10 lead and then lost 39-38 when Eagles kicker Jake Elliott hit a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. Eagles quarterback Joe Milton played by far the best game of his career, throwing for 331 yards, with three touchdown passes and a touchdown run. We've always known Milton had a strong arm, but he showed today that he's more than just a thrower. He can lead an NFL offense as a quarterback. But Dak Prescott is a good quarterback, too, and he turned in a big game of his own. He threw for 291 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions. Prescott's favorite receiver was CeeDee Lamb, who finished with 134 receiving yards, and running back Javonte Williams ran for two touchdowns and also caught a touchdown pass. The Eagles, however, got a monster game from wide receiver DeVonta Smith, who had 11 catches for 200 yards and two touchdowns. Smith was sensational while the Eagles were coming back in the fourth quarter. Special teams miscues killed the Cowboys: The Eagles blocked a punt for a touchdown, and Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal in the fourth quarter. Aubrey, who became the highest-paid kicker in the NFL this offseason, is having the worst season of his career. The loss drops the Cowboys to 5-7 and is devastating to their playoff hopes. The 4-7 Eagles aren't contenders, but they played like contenders today.

title: Emmett Johnson TD gives Chiefs 10-7 lead early in third quarter
summary: The Chiefs got a little something going at the end of the first half.
content: The Chiefs got a little something going at the end of the first half. But they have taken off to start the second. Emmett Johnson punched in a 1-yard touchdown to give Kansas City a 10-7 lead over Buffalo with 11:28 on the clock in the third quarter. The score capped a seven-play, 56-yard drive. Returner Jalen Royals gave the Chiefs a great start with a 37-yard kick return to the Kansas City 44. Then Johnson started the possession with runs of 13 and 12 yards to put the Chiefs in Buffalo territory. A 13-yard pass to Josh Downs put Kansas City at Buffalo’s 1-yard line. Johnson put it in from there. In his third game starting for the injured Kenneth Walker, Johnson now has 53 yards on 11 carries with a touchdown.

title: James Cook touchdown gives Bills 7-0 lead over Chiefs
summary: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night.
content: There is some nasty weather in Western New York on Thanksgiving night. Will one touchdown be enough to win it? The Bills have at least scored one early in the second quarter, with James Cook going in for a 5-yard score. It took Buffalo 11 plays to go 49 yards, with the team getting great field positions as a result of one play on special teams. Chiefs returner Josh Downs let a punt fall and roll instead of fielding it in his team’s territory, which led the offense to start its second drive at the 4-yard line. Kansas City then went three-and-out, and the punt went out of bounds at the Kansas City 49. The Bills only needed to convert one third down on their ensuing drive, with Josh Allen hitting Khaliil Shakir for a 17-yard pass on third-and-6. While Buffalo got down to the 1-yard line, a false start backed them up. but Cook then erased that with his touchdown run. In three drives, Cook has 42 yards on 13 carries with one touchdown. Allen is just 3-of-6 passing for 30 yards.

title: Jeffery Simmons: I didn't simulate snap count on false starts, Lions are "crying" about a them problem
summary: Long before the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second touchdown catch by wide receiver Rome Odunze, one of the storylines of the game was a run of false start penalties by the Lions.
content: Long before the Bears beat the Lions on a last-second touchdown catch by wide receiver Rome Odunze, one of the storylines of the game was a run of false start penalties by the Lions. Center Juice Scruggs was called for back-to-back false starts and then picked up a third later in the half. Left guard Christian Mahogany was flagged for another one before the next snap and there were indications from the Lions that Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was simulating the snap count to get them to jump. Mahogany made that accusation explicit after the game that the Bears "find out the snap count of the quarterback and they use it" while adding that Lions linemen were wearing microphones that he believes will back him up. Simmons was not penalized, but was seen speaking to the referee during a break in play. He denied Mahogany's allegation after the 39-35 win. "We don’t have to . We don't have to," Simmons said, via Dave Birkett of the Detroit Free Press "We line up and play football. They quarterback check. I said, 'Run.' I didn't say, 'Hut.' I mean, their cadence, they say, 'White 80, white 80.' I mean, when you lose football games, it's a lot of complaining and a lot of crying. I mean, there was a couple times that they false start, we didn't say a word. So that's their problem, not ours. . . . If I say, 'Run,' I'm telling my defense, run. Think I care to tell them what they about to do? I'm talking to my guys. So all the crying that they're doing, that's a them problem, not me." Mahogany was flagged for taunting Simmons during a 70-yard Jahmyr Gibbs touchdown run in the fourth quarter and kicker Jake Bates missed the ensuing extra point to leave the score 35-24. The Lions would not score again and the Bears headed back to Chicago with an improbable victory.

title: Jerry Jones on Mike McCarthy: "He was outstanding as the head coach"
summary: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people.
content: The recent remarks from former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers regarding Steelers coach Mike McCarthy have raised plenty of questions, posed to plenty of people. After Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones was asked about McCarthy, who coached Jones's team for five seasons, from 2020 through 2024. "I offered him to stay at least another year when he left," Jones told reporters. "And so I thought he was outstanding as the head coach and had a great command of, frankly, quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's, frankly, one of the finest people that around football that I've been around. And I can't say enough about him. I never had the type of thing that is being said about him. I never had that in consideration in any of my time with him, extending his contract. Any of that, that was never on the table. And we never had an issue within the organization." That conflicts, obviously, with the things Rodgers said on Wednesday. Regardless, Jones no longer employs McCarthy. While Jones possibly chose to take the high road, a former employer vouching for a coach is fundamentally different than his current employer vouching for him. McCarthy took the Cowboys to the playoffs three times in five years, advancing to the divisional round in 2022. The Cowboys failed to qualify for the postseason in the first year after McCarthy left. Thursday's loss to the Eagles makes it harder for them to get there the second post-McCarthy season.

title: Kickers made the difference as Harrison Butker missed, Tyler Bass won the game
summary: The Thanksgiving night game between the Bills and Chiefs was billed as the battle of two great quarterbacks, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes.
content: The Thanksgiving night game between the Bills and Chiefs was billed as the battle of two great quarterbacks, Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. What proved to matter even more was the contrast of two kickers, as Buffalo's Tyler Bass was great and Kansas City's Harrison Butker was not. On a rainy day in Buffalo, the fourth quarter featured Bass making a 54-yard field goal to tie the game 10-10, Butker missing a 46-yard field goal that would have given the lead back to the Chiefs, and then Bass making a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win the game, 13-10. Bass has been excellent this season. He's now 26-for-27 on field goals in 2026, with his only miss coming from 54 yards in last week's win over the Dolphins. Butker has been terrible this season. He's now 15-for-23 on field goals in 2026, and his eight misses are the most for any kicker in the league. He also hasn't made a single kick longer than 50 yards this season; 31 other NFL kickers have made at least one from beyond 50. Chiefs coach Andy Reid said after the loss that he wasn't ready to say whether Butker will remain the kicker in Kansas City. "I'll go back and go through all of it again," Reid said immediately after the game. "Not gonna make any decisions right this minute." It's hard to see how the Chiefs can stick with Butker down the stretch. A kicker's job is to make his kicks, and Butker simply isn't performing.

title: Mike Tomlin on current Steelers situation: "It's a dumpster fire"
summary: Former Steelers coach speaks at length about this week's events.
content: Many folks in and around football have had opinions about the recent brouhaha between former Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and Steelers coach Mike McCarthy. Few have the insight and perspective that former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin brings to the table. Appearing on NBC's Chiefs-Bills halftime show on Thanksgiving night, Tomlin shared his thoughts on the situation in a conversation with Mike Tirico. (A portion of it was on the live broadcast; the full interview is here .) "I had a range of emotions watching those course of events yesterday," Tomlin told Tirico. "I think the prevailing one is just general sadness. Sad on a micro level, sad on a macro level. And by that, I mean, you know, just from an individual perspective, sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career of the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football. So, just a lot of emotions, but probably more than anything, man, general sadness on a lot of levels." Tirico asked Tomlin if he was shocked by Rodgers's decision to air dirty laundry in a public forum. "It certainly did," Tomlin said, "but, you know, and particularly because I know both men involved, certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationship with Aaron over the last couple of years, and have known and competed against Mike, you know, respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time. But I don't — what I acknowledge is I don't know them as a collective, the nature of their relationships, and so certainly I was surprised by that." Regardless of Rodgers's conduct on the way out the door, Tomlin explained that Rodgers was viewed favorably by his teammates in 2025. "He was beloved, and I'm not, you know, over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process, or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real, natural way. He was a tireless worker regarding the process. "I called early-morning quarterback meetings on Wednesday and Thursday. He was always early and engaged. Did a heck of a job in terms of engaging and developing, assisting in the development of young players. Specifically, Will Howard was always in that meeting, and, shoot, man, [Rodgers] and I were shoulder-to-shoulder in terms of the development of Will and challenging Will to develop professional habits. And so, you know, it was early and extremely consistent during my time with him, in terms of his willingness to work in those areas, and I think that's why he's so beloved in that locker room, as been reported by multiple sources in light of this incident. That is real. The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers." Had Tomlin gotten any sense that things were so close to breaking down? "Absolutely none, but it's a really specific reason why, to be honest with you, man," Tomlin said. "One of my cultural mantras, when I worked there for the 19 years, is don't talk to people about your problems unless they can be a component of the solution. Because if you do, it's counterproductive, and people know where I stand there. And by that I mean if you have a problem with your playing time, don't talk to your teammate about it. Talk to somebody that can do something about it. That's problem solving. "And so everybody understands my posture on some of that stuff, and so although I have really good, fluid communication with many of those guys, particularly, the more veteran guys, they know me and know me well enough to know that I didn't want to hear about any potential issues, because I'm not a component of the solution. And so although, particularly, like, Cam Heyward, he and I spent a little time together doing his bye week. Man, we had no mention of anything bubbling under the surface, if you will." Can McCarthy effectively lead the team, given what Rodgers said? "You know, it certainly created some challenges and challenges is probably an understatement if all of those things are true," Tomlin told Tirico. "And certainly the '1-2-3 Packers' is, because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him, or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so, certainly, he's been there a short period of time. And so it makes you wonder, the level of that challenge. But it'll be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned." How does Tomlin think the Steelers will fare against the Broncos on Friday? "Based on my knowledge of the men, particularly the leaders, the longstanding guys, they'll do a great job of getting hyper-focused on what really matters, and that's that football game," Tomlin said. "They'll use it as a mantra to bring them together. I expect those guys to fight. Now, fight and quality play are two different things. I'm certainly not gonna expect those guys not to fight. I think they're gonna fight and fight extremely hard. What I'm interested in is quality of play, quality of execution. And those are things that could be impacted by the level of distraction that they had on a short week in particular." Tirico then asked Tomlin how he feels, overall, about what has transpired this week. "I'm upset about it, you know, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgmental way. I presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset." If owner Art Rooney II calls Tomlin for advice, what would Tomlin say? "Hey, Mike, that's a hypothetical, because I know he wouldn't and, and because I know how he's trained," Tomlin said. "You know, Art is a guy that's not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He's not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team. This is a family business. It's generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, 'What would my dad do?' Or, 'What would my grandfather do?' Their mode of operation is time tested, it's generational. And so, I doubt, very, very seriously, that he called anyone for outside advice." Finally, Tirico asked whether Tomlin believes Rodgers will get another NFL opportunity this season, if he wants one. "There's certainly a possibility for that," Tomlin said. "And I just say that based on the 19 years that I held the position that I held. It's a 32-team league. All it takes is one. Over time, I've laughed and watched that people talk about, you know, 'No, that could never happen.' In a 32-team league, when everybody is highly competitive and there's some real challenges, particularly as you get to this portion of the journey from a player availability standpoint, there's certainly a possibility if he desires that he could play again, because all it takes is one suitor." Having cleared waivers, Rodgers is available to that one suitor, if/when that one suitor calls. Still, that one suitor will need to be willing to accept the risk that, if Rodgers doesn't have things go the way he wants, he'll choose to do again the same thing he did this week.

title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026: Updated AFC and NFC standings, bracket, tiebreakers for Week 12
summary: After an all-time great Thanksgiving for football, the Bears are in first place in the NFC North, the Cowboys have fallen far out of contention in the NFC East, and the Bills are in the lead for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.
content: After an all-time great Thanksgiving for football, the Bears are in first place in the NFC North, the Cowboys have fallen far out of contention in the NFC East, and the Bills are in the lead for the No. 1 seed in the AFC. title: Nick Sirianni is pulled away from fans after comeback win
summary: Good or bad, right or wrong, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has had from time to time the demeanor of a fan who won a contest to be the head coach for a day.
content: Good or bad, right or wrong, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni has had from time to time the demeanor of a fan who won a contest to be the head coach for a day. On Thursday in Dallas, he displayed those qualities after a stunning come-from-way-behind win over the Cowboys. While celebrating the 39-38 win (they trailed 31-10, late in the third quarter), Sirianni approached fans in field-level suites. He eventually had to be pulled away by Dom DiSandro. It's unclear whether he was interacting with Cowboys fans or Eagles fans. He appeared to be making an aggressive movement toward someone before DiSandro intervened. The Eagles contend that Sirianni was celebrating with Eagles fans, and that Sirianni was pulled away so that he could shake the hand of Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer after the game. There was never any contact (at least none that the cameras captured). Still, it's a bad look — and it's definitely on brand. While Sirianni has yet to cross the line, it seems like he will, one of these days. Regardless, the Eagles have now won two in a row after losing seven in a row. They're 4-7 and on the fringes of contention in the NFC East.

title: Tyler Bass hits walk-off 57-yard field goal, Bills beat Chiefs 13-10
summary: Buffalo overcame some nasty weather to once again defeat Kansas City in the regular season.
content: The weather in Western New York delivered nasty conditions with freezing rain for Thanksgiving night. It didn't matter to Tyler Bass. Buffalo's kicker sent a walk-off, 57-yard field goal through the uprights to give the Bills a 13-10 victory over the Chiefs, putting the club further in the driver's seat for the AFC's No. 1 seed. The game was not without controversy, particularly late in the contest. But the weather conditions also affected both teams, as neither offense got much going. Josh Allen finished the game 10-of-21 for 81 yards with two interceptions, rushing for 43 yards on seven attempts. Allen’s passer rating of 18.3 is the second lowest of his career in any regular-season game. Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. James Cook ended up pacing the offense for Buffalo, rushing for 117 yards on 32 carries with Buffalo’s only touchdown — a 5-yard run in the second quarter. The Chiefs got a 26-yard field goal from Harrison Butker to close the first half and a 1-yard touchdown from Emmett Johnson to open the second half. But the team was not able to score again. After Bass connected on a 54-yard field goal in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 10-10, Butker missed his eighth field goal of the year — this one going wide right from 46 yards out. Kansas City had the ball with another shot to get Butker in field goal range. But what looked like a third-down completion from Mahomes to Rahsee Rice was overturned on replay, allowing Buffalo to field another punt. The Chiefs got yet another opportunity to possess the ball after Allen was sacked for the second time on the night. But the club’s special teams continued to have issues, with Josh Downs fielding a punt inside the 10, returning it to just the 11-yard line. And when Mahomes’ third-down pass to an open Kelce fell incomplete, Matt Ariza’s punt was short and skipped to Greg Dortch, who returned 17 yards to the Kansas City 39 with four seconds on the clock. Somehow in the weather conditions, that was enough for Bass, who sent the 57-yard attempt through the uprights to give the Bills their 10th win of the season. Between Butker, Downs’ returns, and Ariza’s punts, the Chiefs special teams had a rough night, arguably costing the team the game. On the injury front, Chiefs receiver/returner Jalen Royals (ankle) exited and was not able to return. With the win, the Bills are now 10-1 and will have at least a one-game lead on the rest of the conference entering Week 13 for the No. 1 seed. Buffalo will play division-rival New England in Week 13. The Chiefs are now 8-3 and won’t have extra rest in the coming week, as they’ll be in Los Angeles to face the Rams next Thursday night.
